the neural network approach to time series analysis is a useful tool for determining the embedding dimension of a data set.

the optimal time delay can be determined by a neural network trained on the data set and that the optimal embedding dimension is the number of time lags that are necessary for a neural network to produce a stable output.

we have proposed a new method for determining the optimal embedding dimension of a scalar time series, and that the method is more reliable than existing methods, especially when the data set has a small number of points or is contaminated with noise.

the development of a neural network based method to determine the optimal time delay and dimension of an attractor for a given time series.
the problem of determining the minimum number of dimensions required to embed a time series into a state-space representation of the system dynamics.
the development of an efficient method for determining the optimal embedding dimension of a scalar time series.

the embedding dimension is not a well-defined quantity, but that it is possible to find a number of embedding dimensions which are good enough for a particular purpose, and that the method proposed in this paper is a convenient way to find such a number.

the embedding dimension of a scalar time series can be determined using a neural network method that compares favorably with conventional methods and that is especially useful when the data are small or contaminated by measurement noise.

the embedding dimension of a chaotic time series is the minimum number of dimensions required to represent the time series as a point on a reconstructed attractor in a space spanned by the time series itself.
